title: Derived internal Hom and evaluation under an isomorphism of coefficient sites
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, with $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible and $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the coefficient-stage operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. At finite coefficients $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ take arbitrary $M,N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. At integral coefficients $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ take $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ with $R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$; the coefficient sheaf is the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. At $E$ take the localized operations on such integral objects, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ take their common finite-field representatives. Write $P=Lg^*$, $H(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom(M,N)$ and $\mu:P(U\otimes^L V)\xrightarrow{\sim}PU\otimes^L PV$ for the canonical tensor comparison.

The evaluation-defined comparison is a natural isomorphism
$$c_{g;M,N}:PH(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(PM,PN).$$
It is characterized by the equality
$$\operatorname{ev}_{PM,PN}\circ(1_{PM}\otimes c_{g;M,N})\circ\mu_{M,H(M,N)}=P(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}).$$
It preserves tensor-Hom transposition: the transpose of $P(b)\circ\mu_{M,L}^{-1}$, for $b:M\otimes^L L\to N$, is $c_{g;M,N}\circ P(b^\sharp)$. These comparisons commute with the canonical cohomological shift identifications and with composition of scheme isomorphisms. At integral coefficients the pullback is identified with the exact inverse-image equivalence on completed module sheaves; its comparison with the tower-defined pullback is the canonical comparison commuting with all reduction projections. The tensor and evaluation comparisons are actual natural maps on the derived categories of reduction systems and their functorial derived-limit realizations, with their specified system evaluation and transposition maps [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; their identities hold there, rather than being inferred from equality of separately evaluated finite-level maps. At the two field stages the displayed maps and identities are the localized and common-stage images, natural also for arbitrary morphisms in the localized Hom groups.

proof.text: Apply the resolution-model lemma at $B_{Y,n}$ and at $R_Y$: its product-Hom isomorphism gives the ambient $c^0$ for arbitrary unbounded inputs, with the prescribed completed coefficient projections. At finite coefficients its derived equivalence is $P=Lg^*$. For the completed coefficient projections, use the already proved projection-normalized isoReductionCompletedMap. Its projection equations give transition naturality, and uniqueness of the limit lift identifies podCompletedRingMap with its isomorphism hom. The exact sectionwise module equivalence then induces an equivalence on the standard derived localizations. For the ordinary finite restriction comparison, identify the completed ring map with isoReductionCompletedMap by the limit projections. Compose the unique comparison of the intrinsic and sectionwise left adjoints with the inverse of the existing restriction square. The left-adjoint comparison preserves units, and the restriction square is identity on sections. For uniqueness cancel the invertible inverse-image unit section maps and use faithful precomposition by the base-change equivalence of sites.

proof.text: The evaluation/coherence lemma identifies this $c^0$ with the unique evaluation-defined comparison. Its transpose formula, signed shifts in both inputs and monoidal compositor equation give all finite-stage identities for the specified $\mu$. Argument-first finite evaluation follows by naturality of the recorded signed braiding, the canonical tensor-pullback braiding square, and the Hom-first evaluation equation. The corresponding inverse tensor square converts argument-first transposition to the Hom-first transpose equation. For the ordinary signed double shift, compose the already proved target shift with the signed source shift from the independent-universe ringed Hom calculus, inserting shiftFunctorAdd' to identify n-m with n+(-m). The two projection formulas give exactly (-1)^(m*k), including negative shifts. Equality transport of the Hom degree handles associativity of the indices; joint monicity of the product projections gives uniqueness of the chain isomorphism.

proof.text: For complete integral inputs the completion-unit/tensor lemma identifies exact inverse image with tower-defined $P$, respecting every reduction projection and both Roos coordinates; it identifies the canonical completed tensor comparison with reindexing. The constructible pullback shift is obtained by conjugating the ordinary exact-derived shift through the complete-input comparison; lift the resulting ambient isomorphism through the fully faithful inclusion. The specified podCompletedToTower map itself is natural by the adjunction-unit naturality square, the inverse limit-reindexing square and the inverse integral-pullback-model square. On constructible inputs its actual unit is invertible by unrestricted normalized reconstruction: translate sf completeness to the legacy complete-object property using any auxiliary prime different from l. The other two factors are already isomorphisms.

proof.text: The reflection lemma extends ordinary evaluation uniquely to completed tensor and restricts $c^0$ to the stated constructible-Hom domain. Under step 3 its naturality, transposition, signed shifts and composition become exactly the integral identities required. More explicitly, compose the reflection lemma’s proved completion-unit Hom bijection with ordinary additive tensor-Hom transposition and the full-subcategory Hom equivalences. Naturality of the actual tensor unit proves parameter naturality; the normalization fixes every transpose and hence gives uniqueness. The ambient signed Hom shift lifts uniquely through the same inclusion.

proof.text: For the system Hom comparison itself, first identify the specified ordinary sequence inverse image with integralComparisonSequencePullback by equality of the coefficient ring maps. The derived identity and composition isomorphisms exhibit pullback by the inverse scheme isomorphism as a quasi-inverse. Closed transposition, full faithfulness, and the specified tensorator make postcomposition with the evaluation-defined Hom comparison bijective on image test objects; essential surjectivity extends this to all test objects and Yoneda gives invertibility. Naturality and transposition follow from the general closed-adjunction calculation. Construct CoreMonoidal from the proved tensorator associativity and unit equations, with its tensor isomorphisms exactly the inverses of the specified comparison; the general finite-coefficient Hom calculation, used purely categorically, supplies internal composition. The system lemma is still used for the untouched commuting square with beta and its total-limit realization, including units and counits; no equality is detected by separate derived finite evaluations.

source.place: Step 5: actual coefficient-system evaluation and reduction square; agent refinement of simultaneous system and total-limit models.

proof.text: For the normalized rational partial closed datum, first construct the transpose by linear base change of the integral transpose and prove naturality by tensor-product induction; then prove uniqueness by equality of inverse transposes on pure tensors. Combine existence and uniqueness to obtain podRationalClosed_existsUnique. The coefficient-descent lemma carries these integral maps and inverses to the localized categories, including arbitrary localized arrows. Its finite-free evaluation normalization and field-tower cocycle make their common-stage classes independent of the field and representatives. Its descended evaluation, transposition, shift and composition identities finish the two field stages.
